finding.claim: Streamable HTTP server does not validate Origin or Host headers, so a DNS-rebinding page can drive an unauthenticated MCP endpoint on a locally bound server (conditional, medium).
finding.source: Web page in victim's browser that DNS-rebinds its hostname to 127.0.0.1; after rebinding requests are same-origin, so no CORS preflight applies.
finding.sink: tools/call and resources/read on an unauthenticated MCP endpoint via server.rb call_tool.

trace.note: call(env) enters the transport with no Origin/Host check
handle_request dispatches POST to handle_post
handle_post begins
Accept header check only; attacker sets the header
Content-Type check only; attacker sets application/json
handle_initialization creates a fresh session without credentials
Mcp-Session-Id returned to attacker
dispatch_handle_json routes the request to the shared server
call_tool resolves the tool by name
tool.call invoked with attacker-chosen arguments

finding.guards_checked: Grep of lib/ finds no Origin or HTTP_HOST check. Accept (:528), Content-Type (:547), and MCP-Protocol-Version (:585) checks are protocol conformance, not origin controls. Session ID is an unguessable UUID, but the attacker creates its own session so it does not help. No auth middleware exists in the library.

finding.claim: POST body is read fully into memory with no size cap before any session or auth check (denial of service).
finding.source: Any unauthenticated POST body of arbitrary size.
finding.sink: request.body.read loads the whole body; JSON.parse then parses it.

trace.note: handle_post entry
request.body.read with no length limit
parse_request_body called on the full string
JSON.parse with symbolize_names; default nesting limit only

finding.guards_checked: No Content-Length or size limit anywhere in lib/. JSON default max_nesting of 100 bounds depth, not size. No auth before read.

finding.claim: Unauthenticated initialize requests can fill the session store, returning 503 to legitimate clients until idle sessions expire (documented trade-off, low).
finding.sink: Session capacity: DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS=10_000 with 1800s idle timeout.

trace.note: DEFAULT_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT = 1800
DEFAULT_MAX_SESSIONS = 10_000
handle_initialization entry
cap check; expired sessions reclaimed only here or by the 60s reaper
too_many_sessions_response returns 503 at cap

finding.guards_checked: Idle expiry and max_sessions cap are present. Reaper interval is 60s (line 83). Attacker sustaining about 5.5 initialize/s keeps the cap full. Source comments document this trade-off (lines 27-34).

finding.claim: Raw exception messages from tool handlers and StandardError are returned to unauthenticated peers in the JSON-RPC error data field (information disclosure, low).
finding.source: Any input that causes a tool or handler to raise, including attacker-triggered errors.
finding.sink: JSON-RPC error response data field sent to the peer.

trace.note: call_tool rescue wraps exception as Internal error calling tool with e.message
handle_request_error sets data = error.message
generic StandardError path sets data: e.message
error_response emitted to peer

finding.guards_checked: Top-level error message is generic (Internal error). Only the data field carries the raw message. No redaction or filtering of exception text.

finding.claim: Full raw request bodies and tool arguments are passed to the configured exception reporter and instrumentation, which can carry PII, tokens, or customer code (data-handling, low; applies only when a reporter is configured).
finding.source: Client-supplied tool arguments and raw POST bodies, which may contain PII, tokens, or customer code.
finding.sink: exception_reporter.call with { request: body_string } and { request: request }; add_instrumentation_data with tool_arguments.

trace.note: handle_post rescue sends full body_string to exception reporter
RequestHandlerError path reports the full request
generic rescue reports the full request
add_instrumentation_data sends tool_arguments unredacted

finding.guards_checked: Default exception_reporter is a no-op (lib/mcp/configuration.rb:163-165), so this applies only when the application configures a reporter. No redaction of payloads in the SDK.
